nodes.statement: Fix closed, connected, topological/PL/smooth 3-manifold conventions and trivial fundamental group.
Topological, PL, and smooth classification of 3-manifolds agree through dimension-three triangulation and smoothing theorems.
A connected simply connected manifold is orientable.
A smooth 3-manifold admits a smooth Riemannian metric, which may be normalized by scaling.
Short-time Ricci flow exists from a smooth initial metric.
Perelman entropy/reduced-geometry machinery yields the required no-local-collapsing and scale control.
High-curvature regions satisfy canonical-neighbourhood and singularity-model conclusions sufficient for surgery.
A Ricci flow with surgery exists for all positive time with a controlled surgery parameter hierarchy.
Crossing a surgery time induces recorded connected-sum decompositions and removal of components from an explicit permitted list.
The simply connected closed case satisfies the finite-extinction topological/group hypothesis without using Poincare.
The relevant Ricci flow with surgery becomes extinct in finite time.
Surgery topology plus extinction reconstructs the initial manifold as a connected sum of spherical space forms and sphere bundles.
Trivial fundamental group eliminates every nontrivial finite or infinite-cyclic factor; remaining spherical factors are S^3.
The smooth input manifold is diffeomorphic to S^3.
The topological input manifold is homeomorphic to S^3.
Elliptization implies the Poincare conclusion by triviality of the spherical deck group.
Geometrization implies elliptization in the finite-fundamental-group case.
Produce a source-complete, dependency-explicit, adversarially audited, and progressively formalizable reconstruction of the Hamilton-Perelman proof.
